chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Sahl ibn Al-Yasa' has been transmitted by me from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far Al-Hamadani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Sahl ibn Al-Yasa'.

key_terms.أَحْمَدَ بْنِ زِيَادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ الْه: Ahmad ibn Ziyad, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect used for narrators.
key_terms.سَهْلِ بْنِ الْيَسَعِ: Sahl ibn Al-Yasa', a companion of the Prophet known for his knowledge of fiqh.
key_terms.عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi, a prominent narrator and compiler of hadith.

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of transmission for narrations from Sahl ibn Al-Yasa' in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq establishes a unified *isnad* (chain of transmission) for all narrations attributed to Sahl ibn Al-Yasa' in this volume, tracing them through Ahmad ibn Ziyad, Ali ibn Ibrahim, and his father to ensure textual consistency. This methodological choice highlights the scholarly rigor of the *Kafi* tradition, where a single reliable chain is often applied to a companion's corpus to maintain authenticity and simplify verification for jurists.
